feed.title: NPR Topics: Politics
feed.subtitle: NPR's expanded coverage of U.S. and world politics, the latest news from Congress and the White House and elections.

entry.title: San Francisco's car crime has plunged. How much credit does Flock deserve?
entry.summary: San Francisco leaders say AI-powered cameras helped drive a dramatic decline in car crime. We examine the evidence — and whether the city can keep its high-tech dragnet without sacrificing civil liberties.

entry.title: Failed 'torturous' execution attempt on Christa Pike reignites death penalty debate
entry.summary: The botched execution in Tennessee of Christa Pike, who survived despite being subject to two doses of lethal injection on Wednesday, has reignited furious debate about the death penalty in the U.S.

entry.title: The U.S. Senate is up for grabs. Can this Ohio Democrat win back working class votes?
entry.summary: After 32 years in Congress, Ohio's Sherrod Brown lost his Senate seat in 2024 as many working class voters turned out for Trump. Now Brown is counting on union voters to send him back to Washington.

entry.title: A judge permanently dismisses former Olympian's Reflecting Pool charges
entry.summary: Citing "exceptional circumstances," a D.C. judge has ruled that the federal government cannot refile its Reflecting Pool charges against David Hearn, despite pressure from President Trump to do so.

entry.title: AI data centers: How much are ratepayers on the hook for?
entry.summary: Data centers consume large amounts of power and require upgrading infrastructure. But it's difficult to determine how much residential customers benefit and how much they actually pay for the benefit.

entry.title: California gubernatorial candidates face off in debate
entry.summary: California's candidates for governor square off in a debate while the blue-leaning state grapples with affordability and other issues.

entry.title: En esta ciudad de Pensilvania, los dos partidos políticos buscan el voto latino
entry.summary: Los republicanos lograron avances con los latinos en el último ciclo electoral, pero la economía y la frustración por la política migratoria de Donald Trump han corroído ese apoyo.

entry.title: COMIC: How the census gives your state power (and what Trump wants to change)
entry.summary: The census is used to determine how much say your state has in Congress and the Electoral College. President Trump failed to alter it during his first term, but he's trying again ahead of 2030.

entry.title: Trade tensions mean fewer Canadians flocking to South Florida
entry.summary: This South Florida community is typically a refuge for Canadians fleeing cold weather, but trade tensions between the United States and Canada mean fewer are coming.

entry.title: Along U.S. Route 1, Maine voters worry about heating oil, gas and Canadian tariffs
entry.summary: Home to both Republican Sen. Susan Collins and Democratic candidate Troy Jackson, Maine's senate race has put rural Aroostook County in the spotlight.
